name: Modelence

plans.name: Free
plans.note: '1 instance, sleeps when idle', 'Shared resources', '1 region'. No cloud usage included and no pay-as-you-go: the free instance is not one of the published container sizes, so sized containers are not priced on Free (sizes_allowed []). App Builder credits are bought separately on any plan.

plans.name: Starter
plans.note: '$20 of cloud usage included, then pay as you go'; 'Up to 4 vCPU across all apps'; 3 regions. The fee is a monthly minimum that is spent on cloud usage (FAQ: 'Each paid plan has a monthly minimum, and the same amount is included as cloud usage every calendar month').

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: '$100 of cloud usage included, then pay as you go'; 'Up to 16 vCPU across all apps'; 17 regions; production autopilot.

plans.name: Scale
plans.note: '$500 of cloud usage included, then pay as you go'; 'Up to 64 vCPU across all apps'; 17 regions; dedicated Slack channel, quarterly architecture review.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: 'From $12,000/yr' (FAQ: 'Enterprise is a yearly contract starting at $12,000'), modelled as a $1,000/mo minimum spent on cloud usage like the other paid plans (whether the contract value is usage credit is not stated). 'Custom vCPU limits', SOC 2, SSO, custom SLAs.

caveats: Free: 1 shared-resource instance that sleeps when idle, 1 region, no cloud usage (not priced here; sized containers start on Starter). Starter $20 / Pro $100 / Scale $500 a month are minimums that include the same amount of cloud usage ('you pay only for the extra usage at the end of the month'); Enterprise from $12,000/yr. Containers billed by the hour by size, e.g. 4 vCPU/8 GB $0.24/h, 4/16 $0.28/h. App Builder credits are bought separately and are not compute.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Per-plan vCPU caps are totals across all apps: Starter 4, Pro 16, Scale 64, Enterprise custom ('Each plan limits the total vCPU across all your apps', https://modelence.com/pricing, 2026-10-14). The largest container is 4 vCPU, so Starter fits one X-Large and Scale at most 16.

Regions per plan: Free 1, Starter 3, Pro and Scale 17 (https://modelence.com/pricing). The homepage names Oregon us-west-2, Montreal ca-central-1, Frankfurt eu-central-1, London eu-west-2 and Tokyo ap-northeast-1 '+12 more regions'; which regions Free/Starter get is not stated, and the US is the default. Regions are kept coarse (us/eu/asia) because 12 of the 17 are unnamed.
Whether a stopped environment stops billing is no longer stated on the pricing page (2026-10-14); usage is 'billed by the hour based on their size'. Large mid-month overage may be billed early.

fleet.tiers: Total vCPU across all apps: Starter 4, Pro 16, Scale 64 (self-serve upgrades), Enterprise custom (yearly contract from $12,000). Free is 1 shared instance.
fleet.notes: Caps are on total vCPU, not instance count: 'If you need more, you can move to a bigger plan, and Enterprise plans get custom limits.' Above 64 vCPU (16 X-Large containers) needs Enterprise.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

secret_proxy.quote: Any variables the user defines in the dashboard under Environment variables.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are environment variables / typed config values of type 'secret' (masked, write-only in the dashboard) injected into the running container at start. No credential-injecting proxy. App Builder LLM usage is paid via platform credits (keys not exposed to user).

isolation.quote: A Docker image built from the repository on an official Node.js image, 18 or newer
isolation.note: Modelence Cloud runs each app as a Docker container built from source; not a VM/microVM product.

image_oci.quote: A Docker image built from the repository on an official Node.js image, 18 or newer (default node-22-slim, set with image).
image_oci.note: The platform builds the container image from the repository's build/start commands; there is no option to push/start from a user-supplied OCI/Docker image.

docker_inside.quote: It needs Docker Compose or a custom Dockerfile to run.
docker_inside.note: Listed as a reason a project is NOT compatible with Modelence Cloud, implying no Docker-in-Docker / Compose support inside the managed container.

nested_virt.quote: Pay only for what you use, based on the number and tier of your app containers
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — a single-process Node.js app container with no documented /dev/kvm or virtualization support.

desktop.quote: Backend, databases and scheduled jobs, deployed and operated by agents
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (a Node.js/MongoDB app-hosting PaaS, not a desktop/VM environment).

browser.quote: Backend, databases and scheduled jobs, deployed and operated by agents
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no managed/embedded browser instance is provided.

computer_use.quote: Backend, databases and scheduled jobs, deployed and operated by agents
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

anti_bot.quote: Backend, databases and scheduled jobs, deployed and operated by agents
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

captcha_solving.quote: Backend, databases and scheduled jobs, deployed and operated by agents
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

ssh.quote: One web process, started with the resource's start commands... You can view logs, metrics, and manage your deployment from the Modelence Cloud dashboard.
ssh.note: No SSH/shell access to the running container is documented; interaction is via the CLI deploy tool and dashboard (logs/metrics/env vars) only.

snapshot.quote: npx modelence deploy ... Build your application / Upload it to Modelence Cloud / Provision necessary resources / Start your application
snapshot.note: Containers are rebuilt from source on each deploy; no disk or memory snapshot/restore feature is documented anywhere on the site or docs.

snapshot_auto.quote: Build your application / Upload it to Modelence Cloud / Provision necessary resources / Start your application

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Build your application / Upload it to Modelence Cloud / Provision necessary resources / Start your application

fork.quote: Pay only for what you use, based on the number and tier of your app containers
fork.note: No machine-cloning feature documented; scaling is done by choosing a container tier/count, not by forking a running instance.

fork_running.quote: Pay only for what you use, based on the number and tier of your app containers

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Pay only for what you use, based on the number and tier of your app containers

pause_resume.quote: Cloud usage is the cost of the resources your apps run on, billed by the hour based on their size. You can change the size and number of instances from your dashboard at any time.
pause_resume.note: The earlier evidence ('you only accrue charges while your deployment is running ... You can immediately stop or adjust your environment at any time') is no longer on the pricing page, and neither the pricing page, homepage nor docs (llms-full.txt) now describe stopping an environment or whether a stopped one is billed. Left unknown.

wake_on_request.quote: Your backend runs as always-on processes, with background workers and scheduled jobs alongside it.
wake_on_request.note: Paid containers do not sleep, so there is nothing to wake. The Free plan's instance 'sleeps when idle' but the pricing page does not say how it wakes.

persistent_disk.quote: What Modelence Cloud runs: A Docker image built from the repository ... Environment variables injected at start: MONGODB_URI and MONGO_URL — a MongoDB Atlas database provisioned for this environment
persistent_disk.note: Modelence Cloud runs the app as a stateless container rebuilt from a Docker image on every deploy; the only stateful pieces are an external managed MongoDB Atlas database (injected via MONGODB_URI) and Modelence Cloud's separate presigned-URL file storage (docs.modelence.com/files.md) — neither is a container-local disk. No docs page, pricing page, or llms-full.txt mentions pause/resume, environment freezing, snapshots, or attachable volumes for the compute container itself; the 'Snapshots / GiB-month' and 'Retained disk / GiB-month' rows in the regime file are generic unverified placeholder billing categories, not evidence of an actual feature. Searched llms-full.txt (14.8k lines) for pause/resume/snapshot/volume/persist/disk/sleep/idle/storage and found nothing describing container-level persistence beyond the external database/file-storage services. Verdict could not be fully proven negative (docs don't explicitly say 'no persistent disk'), hence medium confidence, but no positive evidence for pause/resume-preserved-filesystem, snapshots, or volumes exists to justify the contradiction.

volume_attach.note: No attachable-volume concept in the deploy config or dashboard docs.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Your backend runs as always-on processes, with background workers and scheduled jobs alongside it.
auto_stop_idle.note: Paid-plan containers are always-on and billed by the hour. Only the Free plan's single shared instance 'sleeps when idle' (https://modelence.com/pricing); that instance is not a priced size, so it does not make the priced containers auto-stop.

live_resize.quote: You can change the size and number of instances from your dashboard at any time.
live_resize.note: Container size and count change from the dashboard; no recreate step is described.

agent_harnesses.quote: Set up Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex to build Modelence apps locally
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — the Claude Code/Cursor/Codex integration is for local development tooling (a docs MCP server + plugin) to help write Modelence apps, not a coding-agent preinstalled/offered as a template inside a hosted sandbox.

harness_api.quote: Set up Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex to build Modelence apps locally
harness_api.note: No first-party API to drive a coding harness inside a Modelence-hosted sandbox is documented.

own_agent_api.quote: You can buy Modelence App Builder credits on any plan, including
own_agent_api.note: The App Builder ('Full-stack apps from a prompt') is a prompt-to-app generator paid with separate credits, not a task agent with a first-party driving API.

mcp_server.quote: claude mcp add --transport http modelence https://cloud.modelence.com/mcp ... The same server is available at https://cloud.modelence.com/mcp for tools ... grants access to every app in your organization
mcp_server.note: Modelence ships an authenticated MCP server (cloud.modelence.com/mcp) that reads/manages a user's deployed apps/environments, plus a separate docs-only MCP server.

lang_python.quote: It is not a Node.js application — Java, Python, Go, PHP, Ruby, .NET and so on, even with a Node.js frontend in front. The image runs Node.js only.
lang_python.note: Explicitly Node.js-only runtime; Python apps are stated as incompatible.

public_ipv4.quote: SITE_URL and ROOT_URL — the environment's public URL (both hold the same value).
public_ipv4.note: Apps are reached via a platform-issued/custom-domain URL behind Modelence's load balancing, not a dedicated public IPv4 per container.

ingress_rules.note: Only custom-domain routing is documented; no IP allowlisting, private/auth URLs, or security-group style ingress control for exposed ports is documented.

egress_allowlist.note: No outbound allow/deny list, no-internet mode, or security-group egress rules are documented.

egress_http_rules.note: No HTTP method/path-level egress rule feature is documented.

guest_firewall.quote: A Docker image built from the repository on an official Node.js image
guest_firewall.note: derived: isolation is container (shared-kernel Docker), not a full VM/microVM with guest root, so nftables/iptables control inside is not implied.

static_egress_ip.note: No fixed/static outbound IP feature is documented.

gpu.quote: Size vCPU Memory Price ... Micro 0.25 0.5 GB ... X-Large Plus 4 16 GB
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — pricing lists only CPU/RAM container tiers, no GPU option.

windows.quote: A Docker image built from the repository on an official Node.js image
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Linux-based Node.js Docker images only.

macos.quote: A Docker image built from the repository on an official Node.js image
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Linux container hosting only.

self_host.quote: you are free to replicate your Modelence setup into your own AWS account
self_host.note: Modelence Cloud itself is managed SaaS on AWS. The homepage FAQ says you can migrate off by rebuilding the setup in your own AWS account (standard AWS primitives), which is a manual exit path, not a self-hosted Modelence Cloud. The open-source framework runs anywhere.

byoc.quote: you are free to replicate your Modelence setup into your own AWS account
byoc.note: Migration path only (you then operate it yourself); no managed deployment into a customer cloud account is offered on any plan, including Enterprise.

open_source.quote: LICENSE.md: Apache License 2.0 — Copyright (c) 2025 Modelence, Inc.
open_source.note: The core `modelence` framework/npm package is Apache-2.0 licensed and open source on GitHub; the Modelence Cloud hosting service itself (billing, dashboard, App Builder) is proprietary SaaS built on top of it.

max_session_h.quote: Your backend runs as always-on processes, with background workers and scheduled jobs alongside it.
max_session_h.note: Containers run continuously; no maximum run time is published.

egress_ip_type.quote: Amazon Web Services | Compute, storage and networking that run your applications | Region selected for your environment; United States by default
egress_ip_type.note: Modelence Cloud runs app containers on AWS infrastructure; no static, residential, or mobile egress IP product is documented anywhere on the site or docs, so outbound traffic is ordinary shared AWS datacenter IP space.

arm64.quote: A Docker image built from the repository on an official Node.js image, 18 or newer (default node-22-slim, set with image).
arm64.note: not offered: deploy docs describe only a Node.js base image built and run by the platform with no architecture selection (no ARM64/Apple-silicon/Graviton option is mentioned anywhere in the docs, pricing, or blog).

soc2.note: Listed as a feature of the Enterprise plan ('For companies with security, compliance and scale needs'); not listed on Free/Starter/Pro/Scale. No report or trust page is linked.

hipaa.quote: Special category data | Not required by the Services. If your application collects it, you remain responsible for the additional obligations that attach to it.
hipaa.note: not offered: the DPA explicitly disclaims responsibility for special-category data obligations and no BAA/HIPAA-eligibility offering is mentioned anywhere on the site.

sso.note: Enterprise plan only (dashboard/team SSO); the end-user auth in built apps is still email/password plus Google/GitHub OAuth (docs.modelence.com/authentication).

eu_data_residency.quote: Customer Application Data is stored in the cloud region selected for your environment, which is the United States unless you have chosen another region.
eu_data_residency.note: Region is selectable per environment; the same page's SCC clauses are included specifically for EEA/UK/Switzerland transfers, confirming non-US (including EU) regions are selectable.

custom_image.quote: A Docker image built from the repository on an official Node.js image, 18 or newer (default `node-22-slim`, set with `image`). ... Report the project as not compatible with Modelence Cloud, and say why, when: ... It needs Docker Compose or a custom Dockerfile to run.
custom_image.note: Modelence Cloud only builds its own Docker image from an official Node.js base (chosen from a fixed `node-<version>-<variant>` naming scheme via the `image` config key); a project that requires its own Dockerfile or Docker Compose is explicitly listed as incompatible. There is no way to supply an arbitrary custom container image.

usage_api.quote: You can view logs, metrics, and manage your deployment from the Modelence Cloud dashboard.
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: no; No documented REST API, SDK call, or CLI command for querying billable usage of individual containers or deployments. Billing is per-hour per container tier; usage visibility is dashboard-only (manual viewing, no programmatic access).

locations_quote: Amazon Web Services | Compute, storage and networking that run your applications | Region selected for your environment; United States by default
locations_note: Coarse regions only: 17 AWS regions, of which the homepage names Oregon (us-west-2), Montreal (ca-central-1), Frankfurt (eu-central-1), London (eu-west-2) and Tokyo (ap-northeast-1); the other 12 are unnamed, so no location list (a partial list would rule out regions that may exist). Plans: Free 1 region, Starter 3, Pro/Scale 17.
